learning_objective: 🎯 Discover the VIPs of math: special Prime Numbers that refuse to be broken down by anyone but themselves!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A prime number is a very stubborn number! It can only be divided evenly by 1 and itself. Numbers like 2, 3, 5, and 7 are prime because no other numbers can multiply to make them.
If a number has more than two factors, it is called a composite number. We can break these numbers down into smaller prime pieces using a cool drawing called a factor tree!

fun_activity.title: 🌳 Growing a Factor Tree
fun_activity.instructions: Write the number 24 on a piece of paper. Draw two branches below it with numbers that multiply to 24 (like 4 and 6). Keep branching out until you only have unbreakable prime numbers at the bottom!

quick_recap: ⭐ Prime numbers only have exactly two factors: 1 and the number itself.
⭐ The number 2 is super special because it is the only even prime number!
⭐ Every composite number is just a combination of smaller prime numbers multiplied together.
